title: Price accepts Infinity, 1e400, hex and exponent forms, and becomes null in the posted invoice
evidence: Number('Infinity') is Infinity and passes !(price > 0) at app.js:19. render() then shows 'Infinity' and the total 'Infinity'. JSON.stringify([{price:Infinity}]) writes "price":null at app.js:26. Number('0x10') is 16 and Number('1e3') is 1000, both accepted.
failing_case: Type Infinity (or 1e400) as price, quantity 1, Add line, then Send invoice. The page shows Total: Infinity and the server receives a line whose price is null.
remediation: Parse with one price validator: a strict decimal regex, Number.isFinite, a maximum, and rounding to cents (integer minor units). Reject everything else with a visible error.

title: Double-send guard is a 1-second timer, not an in-flight lock: a slow request can be sent twice
evidence: guards.js:21-26 only compares Date.now() with the last click. app.js:26 awaits the fetch with no flag, no disabled button and no idempotency key. The request succeeds silently (app.js:28), so the user has no sign the first one worked.
failing_case: Click Send invoice; the server takes 3 seconds. The user, seeing no change, clicks again at 1.5 s. tooSoon() returns false, a second POST of the same lines goes out, and the client is billed twice.
remediation: Disable the button and set an in-flight flag until the request settles, and send an idempotency key with the request so the server can reject duplicates. Drop the timestamp guard.

quote: const res = await fetch("/api/invoices", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(lines) });
title: Network failure on Send or Void is an unhandled rejection: the user gets no message
evidence: Only the !res.ok branch is handled (app.js:27, app.js:34). fetch rejects on offline, DNS or CORS failure, and there is no try/catch around app.js:26 or app.js:33. tooSoon() has already consumed the click.
failing_case: Go offline and press Send invoice. fetch rejects, the async handler throws, the console logs an unhandled rejection, and the page shows nothing. The user cannot tell whether the invoice was sent. Retrying within 1 s is also silently blocked by tooSoon().
remediation: Wrap both requests in try/catch, show a visible, announced error that says the invoice was not sent and that nothing was changed, and keep the lines so the user can retry.

quote: const total = lines.reduce((sum, l) => sum + l.qty * l.price, 0);
title: Money is float arithmetic inside render code; price is unbounded and not rounded to cents, so shown lines and total disagree and Infinity is accepted
evidence: app.js:10 computes the total in the view from raw float prices. app.js:18 uses Number(), which accepts 'Infinity', '1e400' and '0x10'; app.js:19 only checks price > 0. app.js:8 displays price.toFixed(2) while app.js:26 sends the unrounded price. Not run (shell was denied): traced from JS semantics (Number('1e400') is Infinity; (0.004).toFixed(2) is '0.00').
failing_case: Enter quantity 1000, price 0.004. The row shows '1000 × 0.00' and the total shows 4.00, and the server receives price 0.004. Enter price 1e400: the price passes (Infinity > 0), the row shows 'Infinity' and the total shows 'Infinity'; that body is then sent by Send invoice (JSON.stringify turns Infinity into null).
remediation: Move pricing to one pure, tested function that parses the price into integer minor units (reject more than 2 decimals, non-finite values and an upper bound), computes line and invoice totals in integers, and have render only display the result; send the same integer values.

title: Whitespace-only client passes the required attribute and is saved as an empty name
evidence: index.html:14 uses required, which accepts '   '. app.js:16 trims to '' and nothing re-checks it before app.js:20. The row then renders an empty link (app.js:8).
failing_case: Type three spaces in Client, quantity 1, price 5, press Add line. A line with an empty client is added; its link has no text and no accessible name.
remediation: Check the trimmed client is not empty before adding, and show the error beside the field.

title: Invalid quantity or price is dropped with no message: Add line appears dead
evidence: app.js:19 returns silently. index.html:14-18 has no error element, no aria-describedby, no aria-invalid, and the qty and price inputs have no required/min/pattern, so the browser adds no message either. index.html:16 uses inputmode only.
failing_case: Type quantity '2.5' or price '' (or '12,50') and press Add line. Nothing is added, nothing is shown, focus does not move. The user cannot tell which field failed or why (WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification, level A).
remediation: On rejection, set a visible text error next to the offending field, mark it aria-invalid with aria-describedby, and move focus to it. Say what is wrong and what is accepted (for example 'Quantity must be a whole number, 1 or more').

title: Send invoice posts an empty invoice when no lines were added
evidence: The handler (app.js:24-29) never checks lines.length; the button is always enabled (index.html:23).
failing_case: Load the page and click Send invoice. POST /api/invoices is sent with body '[]'.
remediation: Disable Send until at least one line exists, and guard the handler with the same check.

title: Successful send shows nothing; sentCount is written and never read
evidence: grep of the payload: sentCount appears only at app.js:3 and app.js:28. After success the lines list and total stay as they were; index.html has no status element.
failing_case: Press Send invoice with 2 lines and a fast server. The page is identical before and after. The user presses Send again after a second and sends a duplicate invoice, or leaves unsure it went.
remediation: On success show a status message ('Invoice sent') in an aria-live region, clear or lock the lines, and remove sentCount or use it for something visible.

title: Void sends no invoice identifier, and the id from Send is never kept
evidence: app.js:26 ignores the response body, so no id is stored; app.js:33 POSTs with no body and no query. Void is also enabled before any invoice was sent (index.html:24).
failing_case: Press Void before sending anything, or after sending two invoices: the server cannot know which invoice is meant, so it voids nothing, the latest, or the wrong one.
remediation: Read the invoice id from the Send response, keep it in state, send it in the void request, and enable Void only when an invoice exists.

title: The whole list is a live region rewritten with innerHTML, so a screen reader re-announces every line on each add
evidence: app.js:7 replaces the full contents of #lines on every render. Total (index.html:22) is an <output> but the validation and send results have no announced region. Traced.
failing_case: With 10 lines on screen, adding the 11th makes a screen reader read all 11 rows again (WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages); errors and send results are never announced.
remediation: Remove aria-live from the list; add a separate role=status element with short messages such as 'Line added: Acme, 2 × 5.00'.

title: Destructive action sits beside Send with identical styling, no confirmation and no undo
evidence: index.html:23-24 two unstyled buttons side by side; styles.css:4 gives all buttons the same look; app.js:31-35 calls the API on the first click.
failing_case: An admin mis-clicks Void instead of Send; the invoice is voided at once with no confirm and no feedback on success.
remediation: Make Send the one primary button, space Void apart in a secondary style, and add a confirm step that names the invoice ('Void invoice 1042? This cannot be undone.').

title: Void invoice is a live-looking button that does nothing for the only user the page defines
evidence: app.js:2 sets roles to viewer and billing; guards.js:10-12 needs 'admin'. The handler returns with no message. index.html:24 renders the button enabled with no explanation.
failing_case: Sign in as sam, click Void invoice. No request, no message, no state change. The user cannot tell if the invoice was voided, or why not.
remediation: If the user lacks the role, do not render the button, or render it disabled with visible text saying that voiding needs an admin; show a message if a click is still refused.

title: Only the browser enforces the admin-only void rule, and the user object is a client-side literal
evidence: guards.js:10-12 canVoid reads user.roles; app.js:2 defines user as a top-level const in a classic script, so it is a global the page visitor can change. app.js:33 posts to /api/invoices/void with no credential, role or invoice id in the request body. No server code is in the payload, so server-side enforcement is not shown anywhere.
failing_case: A viewer opens the console and runs user.roles.push('admin'), then clicks Void invoice. Or they run fetch('/api/invoices/void',{method:'POST'}) directly. The only gate is the browser check, so unless the server independently rejects the call, a non-admin voids an invoice.
remediation: Enforce the admin check on the server for /api/invoices/void from the authenticated session. Treat the client check as display-only, and derive the role from the session instead of a literal.

title: Draft lines live only in memory; a refresh or accidental close discards them
evidence: No localStorage, no beforeunload warning, no server save before Send. app.js:1 is the only store.
failing_case: Add 15 lines, press F5 or swipe back on a phone: the list and total are empty again.
remediation: Save the draft to localStorage (versioned, guarded load, flush on pagehide) or warn before unload.

title: Each row's client name is a link to '#' that goes nowhere
evidence: href="#" with no handler. It is a tab stop and screen readers announce a link; activating it scrolls to the top and adds '#' to the URL. The title repeats the visible text.
failing_case: Tab through the list after adding 5 lines: five focus stops that do nothing, and clicking one jumps the page to the top.
remediation: Render the client name as plain text, or give the link a real target; drop the duplicate title.
